claims.claim_vi: The source presents a possible interview-setting solution with three pipelines: data, blurring, serving.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Data pipeline: annotated dataset with bounding boxes, preprocessing and augmentation (normalised, scaled), train a 2-stage network (steps 1 to 6).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Blurring pipeline: preprocess street view images, detect object boundaries, blur sensitive objects, store in an object store (steps 7 to 10); serving pipeline: users retrieve blurred images (step 11).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The lesson explains a two-stage detector as proposing regions first and classifying/refining them second (the R-CNN family, for example Faster R-CNN, arXiv 1506.01497).
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge, not checked against the primary document in this session (the egress proxy allows GitHub only).

claims.claim_vi: The lesson argues for biasing the threshold toward blurring too much, because a miss leaks private data and a false blur only degrades the picture.
claims.verified_by: Author's reasoning; the source gives no threshold.

design_notes_vi: Khung một là ba đường ống, khung hai là bốn bước làm mờ, khung ba là hai kiểu lỗi.
source_deviations: The source numbers 11 steps; the lesson groups them by pipeline and does not renumber.
The lesson adds why blurring is done offline and the two error kinds (author's reasoning).
The source's title names Google and Apple Maps, but its body calls the design a possible interview solution; the lesson keeps that limit.
The 2009 Google paper on Street View privacy was not opened and none of its results is quoted.
